title: Modi's Personal Yoga Guru Will Lead Times Square on June 21. Here Is What NRIs Need to Know.
excerpt: International Yoga Day 2026 is coming to the Lincoln Memorial and Times Square, with events designed around the health risks that hit South Asians hardest.
body:
International Yoga Day 2026 is shaping up to be the most ambitious celebration yet for the Indian diaspora in the United States. Two weeks before the annual June 21 observance, the stage is already set at two of America's most iconic venues — and the man leading the flagship event is the same guru who guides Prime Minister Narendra Modi's personal practice.

Padma Shri H.R. Nagendra, president of S-VYASA University in Bengaluru and one of India's most distinguished yoga scholars, will serve as chief guest at the Times Square celebration in New York, organised by the Consulate General of India. The event is expected to draw thousands of practitioners from across the country and beyond.

Before the Times Square spectacle, Nagendra will inaugurate a three-day Yoga and Wellness Retreat at the YO1 Longevity and Health Resort in Monticello, New York, from June 12 to 14. The retreat will feature sessions on stress management, healthy ageing, and holistic wellness, alongside lectures by Dr. Samin K. Sharma, Director of Interventional Cardiology at Mount Sinai Hospital.

Meanwhile, the Indian Embassy in Washington has announced that the Lincoln Memorial will host International Day of Yoga celebrations on June 19. "Yoga is the pause button that humanity needs to breathe, balance, and become whole again," Modi said in a statement shared by the embassy.

## This Year's Theme Hits Close to Home

The global theme for 2026 — "Yoga for Healthy Aging" — carries particular weight for the South Asian diaspora. Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death among South Asian Americans, and research consistently shows that South Asians face elevated metabolic risk factors decades earlier than other populations. A growing body of evidence suggests that yoga can help address precisely these vulnerabilities.

A landmark study published in *Integrative Cancer Therapies* found that yoga and pranayama lower stress biomarkers, enhance immune function, and improve quality of life in patients managing chronic conditions. For a community where Type 2 diabetes prevalence runs nearly four times the national average and heart disease risk peaks at age 45, the "Healthy Aging" frame is not aspirational — it is medical.

## The Diaspora Is Driving This

What makes the 2026 celebrations distinctive is not just the venues but the organisational infrastructure. The Rajasthan Association of North America, BRUHUD NY Seniors, and Jaipur Foot USA are co-hosting the New York programme — reflecting a network of diaspora organisations that have worked for years to embed yoga into American public life.

In the Midwest, the Consulate General of India is partnering with local organisations for a free event at the Naperville Yard in Illinois, featuring certified instructor Anu Malhotra leading sessions with live music. Across the Atlantic, Scotland's International Yoga Day celebrations in Glasgow will run a full seven-hour programme of workshops and guided challenges.

## India's Global Push

India's Ministry of Ayush kicked off a 75-day countdown on April 7 with a Yoga Mahotsav at the ancient Lonar crater lake in Maharashtra, where over 5,000 participants performed Trikonasana simultaneously — earning an Asia Book of Records citation for the largest such gathering.

This year's preparations include new yoga protocols designed specifically for air travellers, people managing non-communicable diseases, and participants in the expanded "Yoga 365" campaign, which aims to transform the practice from a once-a-year observance into a sustained daily habit.

## What NRIs Should Know

For diaspora families considering attending, the Times Square event on June 21 is free and open to all. The YO1 retreat runs June 12 to 14 and offers a more immersive experience with medical professionals. The Lincoln Memorial event in Washington is scheduled for June 19. Local consulates across the United States are organising additional events — check with your nearest office for details.

Whether you are a daily practitioner or someone who has not rolled out a mat in years, the 2026 celebrations are designed to meet you where you are. The science says that is exactly the right approach.
